newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money steady,Buba holds policy for now.
newsitem.headline: German call money steady,Buba holds policy for now.

text.p: German call money remained entrenched at the interest rates seen in the previous session, wedged in above the three percent securities repurchase rate in Tuesday's trading.
Dealers quoted call money at 3.05/10 percent, adding that most transactions were taking place at 3.07/08 percent, with fresh tightening seen in the market.

Speculation that the Bundesbank could be close to tightening monetary policy for the first time since 1992 was buoying rates even though the central bank signalled on Thursday that, at least for now, no changes were planned.

The central bank announced a 14-day securities repurchase pact on Tuesday at a fixed interest rate of three percent. While this was entirely expected by the market as the deal had been announced in advance, there had been some speculation that the central bank could set a second pact.

Those in favour of this strategy had argued that a second repo alongside the first one -- most probably at variable interest rates -- would signal to markets that the Bundesbank was prepared to see a small rise in rates on the variable pact.
The central bank's decision to take no such action sent a signal that policy is on hold for now.

The focus now is likely to shift to next week, when the central bank is next due to set a repo tender. Dealers will also be looking closely at the allocation of funds in this week's repo, watching for any sign of a tightening.

Banks' reserve holdings at the central bank totalled 40.8 billion marks on Monday after 41.2 billion on Friday for an average of 41.1 billion marks for the first four days of the month, down from 40.8 billion for the first three days.
Banks took up 300 million marks at the 4.50 percent Lombard rate on Monday, up from 200 million on Friday.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was calculated at and unchanged rate of 3.09455 percent.
